active_release_candidate.purpose: reconcile runtime-only 0.1.28-0.1.30 work into main, repair confirmed regressions, replace model-name context guesses with pre/post model feedback, and re-prove invariants after every invalidating lifecycle transition

current_goal.goal: Restore main as the only development truth and make context/media/UI decisions depend on scoped feedback whose validity is re-confirmed after every lifecycle transition that can invalidate it.
non_goals: Do not change the model-card Video ownership contract.
Do not introduce cross-channel fallback between Ark and Agent Plan.
Do not infer model capabilities or context windows from model names, aliases or broad families.
Do not persist per-instance post-feedback as a permanent global capability table.
Do not claim marketplace or Windows verification from repository CI.

active_validation_frontier.name: feedback_and_lifecycle_closure
next_actions: Re-run the Runtime Distribution Gate for this ready-state HOT-only commit and require the generated runtime artifact to remain valid and equivalent.
Do not publish or merge solely because the candidate is ready; promotion remains a separate explicit release action.
If runtime-affecting code, tests, packaging, README or CHANGELOG change again, demote to validating and re-run the affected evidence matrix.
observed: The first 0.1.31 candidate reached all-green Runtime Distribution, Video, Lifecycle and 0.1.19 workflows, but that evidence did not cover newly identified lifecycle counterexamples.

A real AstrBot 4.27.3 plugin-config hot reload later exposed a genuine state bug: the new plugin instance loaded the new media/cache policy while the already-live Ark Provider was not rebuilt, producing provider_reloads=0.

The hot-reload rebind now selects targets from live instances carrying the plugin-owned marker, obtains their current AstrBot config, and asks ProviderManager.reload() to terminate/load them under the newly imported class; foreign Provider instances are not selected.

The original model-family context mapping was rejected: model identity is not a stable capability proof. The final context design uses current explicit pre-feedback and actual upstream post-feedback; model names are diagnostic labels only.

Successful upstream requests establish accepted lower bounds only. A context rejection revises the next guard only when upstream explicitly reports a context ceiling; unrelated numbers are insufficient evidence.
Explicit output-token reservations are kept outside the derived input-history guard when a reported total context ceiling is translated into AstrBot max_context_tokens.

Learned post-feedback is scoped to the current Provider instance. Provider reload, plugin replacement or AstrBot restart starts again from then-current pre-feedback instead of inheriting old observations as permanent truth.

The first 0.1.31 image guard ran after AstrBot native image Base64 materialization; it has been moved to the image materialization boundary so oversized images are compressed/rejected before Base64 expansion.
Audio transcode output is stat-checked against the configured ceiling before the file is read/Base64 encoded.
Historical 0.1.25 video negative paths remain in an independent blocking test file so new tests cannot erase old evidence.

stable_boundaries: AstrBot owns provider lifecycle, fallback, retry, model-card management, shared Dashboard schema and host model metadata.
The plugin owns Volcengine protocol adaptation and scoped translation of explicit feedback; it must not maintain a second static global capability/context database.
Video remains a native per-model-card modalities choice scoped only to Ark and Agent Plan Source types.
Ordinary Ark and Agent Plan keep separate fixed endpoints and credentials; the plugin never silently crosses channels.
Model identity and model capability are separate: model names, aliases and endpoint IDs never determine context limits by themselves.
Pre-feedback is current request-before evidence from the concrete object/host state; post-feedback is evidence from the actual upstream request outcome.
Successful post-feedback establishes only an accepted lower bound; an explicit upstream ceiling is required to revise a context ceiling/guard.
Post-feedback may constrain the next request inside the same Provider lifecycle but does not become permanent global model truth.
A confirmation is valid only for its object/state/lifecycle node; transitions that can invalidate it require a new confirmation.

A proven HOT-only state transition may inherit runtime/UI evidence only when the Runtime Distribution Gate proves the generated runtime artifact is unchanged in semantics and remains valid; any runtime-affecting change reopens validation.
Older negative-path contracts remain independently executable when later releases add new tests.
Runtime is generated from main; direct runtime development is not an accepted steady state.
warning: 0.1.31 is ready as a release candidate but is not yet published or user-installable. Stable user installations remain on runtime 0.1.30 until an explicit guarded promotion updates runtime.
